content: 1. Ritonavir reduces the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Protease inhibitors, including ritonavir, have been associated with the onset or worsening of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia. 2. Lopinavir reduces the effects of albiglutide through mechanisms not fully understood. Similarly, ritonavir decreases the effects of albiglutide. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Reports suggest that protease inhibitors may induce hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. 3. Both lopinavir and alfuzosin increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 4. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of amikacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 7. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by both inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, ritonavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 10. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir has a similar effect. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration of apalutamide with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require initial dosage modification, but dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. 11. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, lopinavir increases the levels or effects of aprepitant. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 13. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Ritonavir and lopinavir affect the metabolism of artemether via CYP3A4, potentially increasing or decreasing its levels. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 16. Ritonavir decreases the levels of artesunate by increasing its metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of its active metabolite (DHA). Monitor for decreased efficacy. 17. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The recommended dosage of atogepant with OATP inhibitors is 10 mg or 30 mg once daily. 19. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of atomoxetine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atorvastatin increases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Azithromycin increases the levels or effects of ritonavir via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, ritonavir also decreases their levels by increasing metabolism. Reduced bazedoxifene exposure may increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 23. Lopinavir and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring, including ECG, are required. 24. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are essential. 25. Ritonavir increases the levels of berotralstat via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Similarly, lopinavir increases berotralstat levels. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Lopinavir increases the levels of betrixaban via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ritonavir has a similar effect. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, followed by 40 mg daily when co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. 27. Ritonavir decreases the levels of bexagliflozin by inducing UGT1A9 metabolism. Consider adding another antihyperglycemic agent for patients requiring additional glycemic control. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 28. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir has a similar effect. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Bosutinib increases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir has a similar effect. Monitor patients for adverse reactions. 32. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 inhibitors. If both inhibitors are used, administer a quarter of the dose. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 33. Ritonavir increases bromocriptine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 34. Budesonide decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, ritonavir increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase buprenorphine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required due to the potential for increased toxicity. 36. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase buprenorphine buccal and subdermal implant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for signs of overmedication. If CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and patients should transition to a buprenorphine formulation that allows dose adjustments. 37. Ritonavir decreases bupropion levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Bupropion levels may decrease by 20-80%, and dose adjustments may be required. Caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Ritonavir increases buspirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 39. Butabarbital decreases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Butalbital decreases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary.
